claims.content: Customer wants to browse and search products by using available filters and search criteria to find the items they are looking for.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Customer browses and searches products, narrowing results by filter criteria to locate desired products.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Customer initiates browsing/searching, supplies or selects one or more filter criteria, and the system returns the products matching those criteria for the customer to view.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer begins a browse or search session for products.
scope_contract.success_boundary: System has presented the matching product results to the customer based on the specified browse/search criteria.
in_scope_actions: Apply filters/search criteria to narrow results
excluded_adjacent_actions: Managing inventory or auctions as an administrator
Downstream processes not part of browsing/searching and viewing product results
variant_dimensions: Filter/search criteria: Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location, Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Cost Range

claims.content: Customer
The system has inventory data populated and available for the Customer to browse and search.

Customer initiates a product browse/search session by entering a Product ID (e.g., ABC123) or Customer Email Address and clicking the 'Go' button, or by selecting one or more search parameters such as Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, and Cost Range and clicking the 'Find Product' button.
The Customer uses the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability to browse the product inventory.
The Customer specifies one or more search/filter criteria, using direct entry or selection from filter lists, and these criteria can be combined to narrow the product results.
The Customer executes the search by clicking the 'Go' or 'Find Product' button.

The system displays the search results in the relevant view: a table titled 'Search Results' containing columns for Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment, with rows showing matching auction items; for Product ID searches, a 'Search Results for Item' section containing columns for Auction Status, Auction_Seq, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve, High Bid, # of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder; and, when multiple items are found, a category/search result page using the default catalog view, where each item is represented by a Product Module containing a thumbnail image, description, countdown timer, current high bid, and QuickBid button.
The displayed search results include thumbnail images for each item and can be sorted by clicking underlined column headers.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of using the Endeca search/navigation capability, the Customer may access product browsing via a Site Map page listing all available Categories (Jewelry, Gemstones, Collectibles, Watches), Product Types (e.g., Rings, Necklaces, Bracelets), and Gemstone Types (e.g., Tanzanite, Diamond, Ruby) as direct links to specific pages or Endeca results pages.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of using the Endeca search/navigation capability, the Customer may enter product browsing via SEO-optimized landing pages focused on specific gemstone types (e.g., 'tanzanite page') or product types (e.g., 'Rings page'), which contain direct links to relevant product categories such as 'all loose tanzanite stones' or 'all tanzanite rings'.

Diverges from Step 2: When specifying search/filter criteria, the Customer may use radio buttons to choose between viewing only 'Items currently online only' or 'All sellable auction inventory'; this scopes the results without impacting the 'Red status' columns.

Diverges from Step 2: The Customer may use combinable radio-button filter options to enable viewing items with or without images, and with or without a valid (sellable) location, altering the composition of the result set.
Diverges from Step 4: The Customer may switch the presentation of product results between 'List View' and 'Catalog View' display modes.

Diverges from Step 4: The Customer may group results using a scrolling list box with options including Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material, Material Purity, Product Group, Brand, Inventory Realm (Red, White), Inventory Aging Bucket, J/G Score, and Ring Size; each grouping option generates corresponding columns in the Results section.
Diverges from Step 5: Instead of sorting by underlined column headers, the Customer may sort the product results by 'Current Price: low to high' using a dropdown menu.

Diverges from main_flow step 1: If the Customer clicks a link/category that contains no product (which happens routinely for collectibles), the system serves a 'no results found' page; the branch exits to that no-results page.

Diverges from main_flow step 4: If the search yields no matches, the system displays a 'No Results Found' page instead of the Search Results table; the page includes an apology message, a 'Search Tips' section with five suggestions (check typos, remove unnecessary words, try plural/singular forms, use fewer/generic keywords, contact support), and a 'May We Suggest' section containing static popular gemstone and jewelry searches plus dynamically updated search terms/phrases using Omniture data; the branch exits to this no-results page.

Diverges from main_flow step 4: The system excludes any product without an available image from appearing on product details pages, search results, or catalog pages; this hard pre-filter can leave the result set empty or incomplete even when other criteria match, and such products are omitted from the displayed results.
The system has presented the matching product results to the Customer based on the applied browse/search criteria.

The system displays a search results table (titled 'Search Results') with columns in default order: Action (checkbox), thumbnail image, Product ID (SKU #) with link to SKU History page, Auction ID, Description, Opening Bid, High Bid, Item Unit Cost, Start time, End time, Duration, Product Type, and Increment; Start time, End time, and Duration are initially blank.

When the search is for a specific Product ID, the system displays a 'Search Results for Item' section containing a table with columns Auction Status, Auction_Seq, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve, High Bid, # of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder, populated with rows corresponding to the matching auction history.

When results are displayed in product-module/catalog view, each product in the filtered list is represented by a Product Module showing a thumbnail image, a short description (On-Air Description), a countdown timer in D:HH:MM:SS format, the current high bid, and a QuickBid button.

quality_flags.detail: [trigger_preconditions_coverage] The Trigger explicitly allows the Customer to initiate a search by entering a Customer Email Address and clicking 'Go', but Preconditions only asserts that inventory data is available. A Customer Email Address search also requires the system to have customer-email-to-product/auction lookup data (or equivalent customer profile data) available; that independent data state is not represented in Preconditions, so the Trigger is not fully covered. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The cited evidence does not specify that customer-email-to-product/auction lookup data or equivalent customer profile data is populated/available; it only documents that Customer Email Address can be entered to initiate a search.))

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The Trigger explicitly allows the Customer to initiate a search by entering a Customer Email Address and clicking 'Go', but Preconditions only asserts that inventory data is available. A Customer Email Address search also requires the system to have customer-email-to-product/auction lookup data (or equivalent customer profile data) available; that independent data state is not represented in Preconditions, so the Trigger is not fully covered.

inconsistency_hints: The Main Flow's only result-display step is the generic 'Search Results' table. Postcondition 3 requires a distinct 'Search Results for Item' section for Product ID searches, and Postcondition 4 requires a product-module/catalog view; neither state is introduced or reached by the Main Flow, so the flow does not lead to these postconditions.
